principles.title: Data is never instructions.
principles.body: Every service I build hands the model what a person said as a claim with provenance, not as a command. Four of the LUCY services make that an ADR with a test behind it.

principles.title: The sandbox is the feature.
principles.body: Environments-api is remote code execution as a product, so path containment, PID ownership and sandbox tiers come first and the polish comes after.

principles.title: Every gate, everywhere.
principles.body: Lint, types, imports and tests at 100% branch coverage, the same four checks in every family repository, with a parity script that notices when one drifts.

experience.title: Founder and sole engineer
experience.summary: Design, build and ship the REX product line: the LUCY assistant hub and its service family, the weftai workflow runtime (npm and PyPI), Android Headless Mirror, Flint, textwire, chika and clyde. Every repository carries the same gates and the same visual system.

projects.name: LUCY
projects.tagline: An assistant hub with a family of eight services behind it.
projects.description: Lucy is the hub: health, readiness, identity, sessions, a durable conversation runner, resumable event streaming, capability packs, child helpers, watches, MCP in both directions and a command-line client. It turns a request into a plan of named operations and feeds earlier results into later steps by reference, so the model never copies an identifier. Memory, persona and pinned account facts reach the model as separate sections whose retrieval scores are never merged.
highlights: Durable conversation runner with resumable event streaming
Declarative plans: steps reference earlier results as $hits, not copied text
MCP server and client in the same hub
Any catalogued provider or a local runtime; lucy talk from a terminal
make check runs the same four gates in all nine family repositories

projects.name: weftai
projects.tagline: Composable AI workflows: the model plans, your code executes, results never travel through the model.
projects.description: A model emits a declarative plan of named steps. Your application validates it against Zod schemas and runs it. Results flow between steps by name and stay in a session-scoped store, so one tool call can chain three dependent lookups with zero identifiers copied by the model. Published as five npm packages under one version and as the same library on PyPI, with the same plan format.
highlights: One tool call, three dependent lookups, zero identifiers copied by the model
Operations defined once: name, description, Zod input schema, output type, handler
Previews for the model, full sets for the code; positions index the full set
npm (weftai, @weftai/*) and PyPI releases from one versioned monorepo
Property-based tests with fast-check, Biome, changesets

projects.name: Android Headless Mirror
projects.tagline: Your Android phone, in one window on your Windows PC, with its own screen off.
projects.description: Plug the phone in and it appears on screen. The app waits in the tray, opens when an authorised phone connects and restarts the mirror if it crashes. Two fingers on a Windows Precision Touchpad become two fingers on the phone. A GPU-rendered soft background, a live navigator, phone controls and phone settings all live in a single window, with a first-run tour and a CLI. Every release ships with a signed-off website, 26 Playwright site tests and UI Automation tests against the real window.
highlights: Real touchpad gestures mapped to the phone: pinch, rotate, pan
Blurred live background rendered on the graphics card at 60 fps
Per-user installer, no admin rights, scrcpy bundled, auto-update
Repository rules that keep the site, the app and the CLI in agreement
Seven more features planned across twelve PRs, ~150 settings

projects.name: Flint
projects.tagline: Cast a PC screen to a Fire TV at the lowest latency the hardware allows.
projects.description: A Windows host and a Compose-for-TV receiver. Desktop Duplication capture, colour conversion and downscale on the GPU's video processor, hardware H.264 encode, and a receiver that decodes and renders it, proven end to end on a Fire TV Stick. The REX wire protocol is implemented in Rust, C# and Kotlin and held byte-identical by a committed cross-language vector corpus. A capability prober reports, per device pair, which modes are actually possible, and the UI never presents an unavailable mode as a working control.
highlights: GPU capture, convert, downscale and hardware encode on Windows
Fire TV receiver in Compose for TV: remote-operable, overscan-safe
One wire protocol in Rust, C# and Kotlin, checked by golden vectors
Authenticated, read-only ADB identification honouring the TV's consent prompt
Rolling releases; self-updating per-user installer with no .NET to install

projects.name: textwire
projects.tagline: Browse the web and search from a phone with no data connection, over plain SMS.
projects.description: The phone texts a request to a number the server owns. The server fetches the page or runs the search, reduces it to readable text, compresses it with a trained zstd dictionary and sends it back as numbered SMS frames. The app reassembles them, asks again for any that went missing, and shows a clean, tappable page. Built and tested end to end in process, including lost and reordered texts, and runnable with no phone and no account.
highlights: Trained zstd dictionary and a framed wire format with golden vectors
Retransmission of lost and reordered SMS frames
make simulate runs the real server against a virtual phone, sends nothing
A hard daily SMS budget caps the cost of any mistake
Landing page and handbook built from the repository's own Markdown

projects.name: Chika
projects.tagline: An agentic assistant with full browser control, installed like a real app on Windows, macOS and Linux.
projects.description: Chika reads your open tabs, navigates pages, extracts data, takes screenshots and answers questions about anything you can see in Chrome, powered by Claude, GPT-4o or other providers. Each platform gets a real installer and a real uninstaller, per-user with no admin rights, and the CLI auto-updates on launch when upstream CI is green. A one-command extension install gives it hands in the browser.
highlights: Chrome extension: read tabs, navigate, click, screenshot, watch for changes
Native installers for Windows, macOS, Debian and any Linux distro
Auto-update gated on green CI; chika doctor verifies the install
Provider and key setup in-app, changeable at any time

projects.name: clyde
projects.tagline: The Claude Code CLI as an OpenAI-compatible model provider on localhost.
projects.description: Point anything that speaks POST /v1/chat/completions at it and the replies come from claude -p under your own login, with no API key. It is deliberately not an agent: every call runs with no tools, no MCP servers, no skills and an empty working directory, and that lockdown is checked at startup rather than assumed. /ready reports exactly what the probe saw load and refuses every call until it was nothing.
highlights: OpenAI wire format: /v1/models, /v1/chat/completions, JSON schema answers
Startup probe proves the lockdown; refuses calls otherwise
Loopback only, documented as such
Design doc records the measurements that chose each CLI flag

projects.name: keyring
projects.tagline: Accounts, profiles and credentials: the vault the rest of the family authenticates against.
projects.description: One person logs in once. Their profiles hold the credentials for third-party services, and any service that needs one asks keyring for a usable credential at the moment it needs it: a refreshed OAuth token, an API key, or the fields for a login form. No other service stores a secret, and no endpoint ever hands a stored secret back out.
highlights: OAuth consent flows and token refresh on behalf of a person
Internal credential resolution for services acting for a person
Master-key encryption at rest

projects.name: memory
projects.tagline: Where what an assistant learns about a person goes, with provenance, confidence and corrections.
projects.description: A memory is a remembered claim with everything needed to judge it later: who asserted it, where it came from, how confident the writer was, when it was true and whether it has since been corrected. Episodes, facts, procedures and summaries; account, profile and session scopes; stated, observed, inferred and untrusted trust levels.
highlights: Four kinds, three scopes, four trust levels
Episodes stay in their session; facts cross sessions
Everything shown back to the person it is about

projects.name: persona
projects.tagline: Somewhere for an assistant to keep a model of itself and get it back later.
projects.description: A small identity card plus two kinds of knowledge the assistant writes for itself: typed fields it defines and fills, and free-text notes. Both are searchable, carry provenance and can be pinned into the identity block loaded at the start of a turn. One persona per profile, so a work assistant and a home assistant are different people. Four rules, each an ADR with a test: a persona is data, never instructions.
highlights: Assistant-defined schema that grows as it learns
Pinned identity block per turn
Four ADRs enforced by tests

projects.name: user
projects.tagline: Structured data about the person an assistant is talking to, returned as claims with provenance.
projects.description: Preferred name, timezone, household, allergies, what they are working on, what they said last month. Everything comes back with provenance so it can be rendered as a claim rather than obeyed as an instruction; anything that looks like a credential is refused rather than stored; forget that reaches the bytes on disk; and no request can name a person other than the one its token was minted for.
highlights: Credential-shaped values refused
Delete means the bytes on disk
Token-bound: no cross-person access

projects.name: settings
projects.tagline: One place a person decides how every service in the family behaves for them.
projects.description: Which country music searches resolve against, how long an idle workspace stays up, which model answers, which providers must never see a query. Decisions that belong to the person, lifted out of environment variables that applied to everybody on the box.
highlights: Per-person, per-service settings over HTTP
settings-client consumed by the other services as a tagged source

projects.name: environments
projects.tagline: Sandboxed environments and shells, as an API. Remote code execution as a product.
projects.description: Creates isolated workspaces, runs shells in them, reports what is running and lets an assistant kill or wait on it. Because it executes arbitrary commands for remote callers, the sandbox tiers, path containment and PID-ownership checks are the feature, not polish.
highlights: Sandbox tiers reported by /ready
Path containment and PID ownership checks
Authenticates against keyring; per-person settings

projects.name: spotify lookup
projects.tagline: Resolve batches of loosely specified tracks against Spotify, and control playback with every command confirmed on the device.
projects.description: Submit an array of { name, artist?, album?, year? } and get back one fully populated result per item, in order, each with its own status. It holds no Spotify credential of its own: every request carries the caller's keyring token and keyring hands over the headers for that person's own connection. 100% coverage.
highlights: Batch, order-preserving resolution with per-item status
Playback commands confirmed on the device
No credential of its own

projects.name: web search
projects.tagline: Scrape search results and pages, then synthesise an executive summary with any of 54 LLM providers.
projects.description: A FastAPI service that scrapes Google results and web pages and summarises them with local Ollama, every Anthropic and OpenAI model, and 51 more that speak OpenAI's wire format. API only, designed to sit behind an MCP server. Provider keys never live here; they are resolved per request from keyring for the person the request is for.
highlights: 54 providers behind one interface
Per-caller credentials, so answers are per caller
Local runtimes work with no keyring at all

projects.name: AI Context Bridge
projects.tagline: Carry a conversation from ChatGPT to Claude to Gemini and back, in seconds.
projects.description: A Chrome extension that saves chat history from any of five AI platforms and injects it into another. Shadow DOM isolation keeps the injected UI clear of host styles; LZ-string compression keeps long conversations under a 5 MB cap; the save button disables while the AI is still generating; and every platform has ordered selector fallbacks against DOM changes.
highlights: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and Grok: extract and inject
Native value setter and synthetic events for React and Vue inputs
Keyboard shortcuts, JSON import and export, UUID de-duplication

projects.name: Mary-Jo Corporate Events
projects.tagline: A static client site with a branded contact form that posts to Google Apps Script.
projects.description: A static Nuxt, Vue and TypeScript website for a corporate events business. The branded contact form is built into the static site and posts to a Google Apps Script web app in production, with a local fallback route for development. Typecheck, lint, unit and end-to-end tests.
highlights: Nuxt static generation
Serverless contact form via Apps Script
Playwright end-to-end tests

projects.name: CodeConnect

projects.description: An early full-stack project: file hosting with a real-time search bar built on Levenshtein similarity, customisable HTML documentation sections, rendered code boxes with copy buttons, a node registry for CLI installs, collaboration, chat and a user dashboard.
highlights: Levenshtein-based live search
User-authored documentation templates
